name: King T
notes: First-generation Compton crew rap crossing into 90s West Coast funk, and its one load-bearing balance decision is that the drums are louder than the melody — the research says "hard, upfront drum balance (louder drums relative to melody than the Death Row template)", so this model runs the busiest kick and the thinnest melodic layer of the LA half of this batch, with `percs.gainOffsetDb` pulled up to -4 where the genre sits at -7. Swung 16ths, a fat sample-derived snare and breakbeat kick placement give it `syncopation` 0.52 and `offbeat8thShare` 0.30 over the genre's 0.50/0.35. Harmony is genuinely incidental — "funk-modal single-chord vamps" with the loop, not played keys, supplying it — so `impliedByRiff` is set and `extensions.triad` is 0.74, the plainest voicing in this batch. ⚠ `medium` is the research's own rating. The INFERRED parameter is `chords`: nothing documents a progression, so the single-`i` family carries almost all the weight, `chordDurationBeats` [2,12] plus three harmonic rhythms carry the variety the chord part owes, and the i–VII family is inference from "funk-modal" alone — it is the first thing to delete if this ever sounds busier than the records. ⚠ Scratched vocal samples used melodically have no lane; the horn/organ hook motif is the modelled voice instead. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 47 to 45 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 46 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 2. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [2,1], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
